Design9795 · aluminium winding · Al end-winding multiplier 1.136

Summary

Aluminium end-winding multiplier 1.136

The copper reference is Design9795_1 as given, with Motor-CAD's armature end-winding MLT multiplier 0.7 (mean turn 203.6 mm, 13.48 mΩ per path, 6.74 mΩ phase, 4.49 mΩ line to line at 100 °C). Every aluminium winding uses a multiplier of 1.136: the end-winding part of each aluminium turn is 1.623 × longer than at 0.7. The copper-size drop-in, for example, goes from 203.6 to 250.7 mm mean turn and 27.49 mΩ per path. Everything else (fields, iron loss, prices, vehicle, criteria) is as in the 0.7 study.

Aluminium can replace the copper winding of Design9795_1 with stator-only changes (rotor cross-section, magnets, air gap and M235-35A kept), but not at equal efficiency within the 167 mm OD limit. The best balance saves ₹952 per motor (22 % of active-material cost) for 1.96 % range.

Recommended · OD 167 · 74 mm

−₹952

Range -1.96 % (telematics), -2.38 % (WMTC). Stator F4 (OD 167, yoke 6.85 mm, slot 23.15 mm deep, tooth 14.54 mm), 74 mm stack, 9 turns × 4 × 1.90 mm Al. Torque within 0.8 % of copper at every speed, +0.44 kg. Winding loss at peak torque +19 %.

Alternative, 98.8 % torque at high speed · OD 167 · 72 mm

−₹992

Range -1.86 % / -2.10 %. Stator F2 (OD 167, yoke 7.85 mm, slot 22.15 mm deep, tooth 15.54 mm), 72 mm stack, 9 turns × 5 × 1.60 mm Al. Winding loss at peak +32 %, +0.41 kg.

Least range loss · OD 167 · 78 mm

−₹696

Range -1.54 % / -2.01 %. Stator F1 (OD 167, yoke 8.85 mm, slot 21.15 mm deep, tooth 15.54 mm), 78 mm stack, 8 turns × 6 × 1.50 mm Al. Winding loss at peak +16 %, +1.19 kg.

Method and copper baseline

Every number comes from the Motor-CAD-equivalent FEMM model of Design9795_1, extended with FEMM solutions of each stator variant, then run through the vehicle drive cycles.

StageScriptWhat it computesCount
1. Copper modellab_model.py (v3), make_lab_v2.pyMotor-CAD-equivalent Lab model: skew slices, Motor-CAD torque, minor-loop hysteresis + harmonic eddy iron lossvalidated on 840 Motor-CAD map points
2. Stator variantsalu9795_femm.py (FEMM)Torque, d-q flux, stator iron-loss sums, slot field, tooth and yoke flux density on a 4 × 4 current grid × 2 rotor positions17 stators × 32 = 544 solves
3. Design searchalu9795_study.py, alu9795_search.pyEach stator × stack 64–90 mm × 8/9/10 turns per coil × 1–6 strands: envelope, efficiency map, peak point, drive cycles, cost4285 designs
4. Best designsalu9795_analyse.pyCost against range fronts per OD and criterion; Al price sensitivity4 ODs × 2 criteria × 3 prices
5. FEMM checkalu9795_verify.pyDirect solves between grid nodes, 4 rotor positions, against the interpolation60 solves
6. Operating pointsalu9795_ops.pyOP1–OP3: currents, phase advance, voltage, flux, power factor, loss breakdown13 designs

Copper baseline (Design9795_1)

Stator OD 160 mm, bore 107 mm, 12 slots, slot depth 17.65 mm, tooth 15.54 mm, yoke 8.85 mm, slot 281.2 mm²; 10-pole spoke ferrite rotor; 64 mm stack; delta, 2 parallel paths, 10 turns per coil of SWG 11 (2.946 mm) copper, fill 0.513; M235-35A. Drive: 52 V, modulation 0.95 (49.4 V phase peak), 360 A rms line, 280 A DC, MTPA. Winding and magnets at 100 °C.

Aluminium end-winding multiplier 1.136

The copper reference is Design9795_1 as given, with Motor-CAD's armature end-winding MLT multiplier 0.7 (mean turn 203.6 mm, 13.48 mΩ per path, 6.74 mΩ phase, 4.49 mΩ line to line at 100 °C). Every aluminium winding uses a multiplier of 1.136: the end-winding part of each aluminium turn is 1.623 × longer than at 0.7. The copper-size drop-in, for example, goes from 203.6 to 250.7 mm mean turn and 27.49 mΩ per path. Everything else (fields, iron loss, prices, vehicle, criteria) is as in the 0.7 study.

The FEMM copper model matches Motor-CAD Lab within 0.28 efficiency points (mean over 840 map points), 1.6 % torque and 2.7 % total loss; envelope torque within 0.7 % from 1000 to 9000 rpm (see the Lab validation report).

Motor-CAD values from its envelope export (OP1, OP3). Motor-CAD splits iron loss into stator/rotor and hysteresis/eddy for the machine; its OP1 hysteresis 111 W, eddy 184 W. FEMM's OP1 iron loss is lower (the known hysteresis gap), so copper's FEMM efficiency is +0.46 points against Motor-CAD at OP1 and +0.08 at OP3. Aluminium designs are compared with FEMM copper, so this offset cancels.

How an aluminium design is evaluated

  • Turns: currents scaled by turns (same ampere-turns give the same field), flux linkage × turns, end-winding inductance × turns².
  • Stack length: flux, torque, iron loss and windage scale with length (2D); end-turn length unchanged.
  • Stator variant: FEMM differences against the copper stator at the same ampere-turns, added to the copper model (flux), or as ratios (stator iron loss, slot field). Checked against direct FEMM solves: ψq within 0.88 %, iron-loss ratio within 1.6 %.
  • Winding: aluminium EC-1350 (2.826 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m at 20 °C, 0.00403/K, 2703 kg/m³) at 100 °C; insulated fill at or below copper's 0.513; IEC and SWG wire sizes from 1.0 mm, 1–6 strands; mean turn = 2L + end turn corrected for tooth width and coil thickness; AC loss by Motor-CAD's hybrid method (factor 2) with FEMM's slot field.
  • Acceptance: full = peak torque ≥ 99.5 % of copper and envelope ≥ 99 % at every speed 0–9500 rpm; relaxed = envelope ≥ 97 % (shortfall only in the DC-power-limited region above about 3000 rpm).

Design9795 · aluminium winding · Al end-winding multiplier 1.136

OD 160 mm

Same OD and housing as copper. The slot can only grow inward (thinner yoke) or sideways (thinner teeth), and both cost torque per ampere-turn: −1.3 % per mm of yoke, −1.9 % per mm of tooth. Aluminium therefore needs a long stack. 1765 designs evaluated at this OD; 100 keep full torque at every speed, 656 stay within 3 %.

OD 167 mm

Design9795 · aluminium winding · Al end-winding multiplier 1.136

Comparison across ODs

A larger OD moves the whole cost-range front up and to the right: each mm of OD adds 0.5 mm of slot depth (about 11 mm² per slot) for about 0.06 kg (₹18) of stator steel. That is cheaper than adding stack length, which also lengthens the rotor and magnets.

What each lever does

ChangeGainCost
OD +1 mm (yoke and tooth kept)Slot +0.5 mm deep, +11 mm²; torque per amp −0.1 %+0.06 kg stator steel (₹18); new die and housing bore
Yoke −1 mmSlot +1 mm deep, +22 mm²Peak torque −1.3 % (yoke B 1.70 → 1.78 T)
Tooth −1 mmSlot +15 mm²Peak torque −1.9 %; tooth saturates earlier
Stack +2 mmTorque and flux +3 %; resistance per N·m falls+₹83 to ₹86 stator steel, rotor laminations and magnets; iron loss and windage +3 %
10 → 9 → 8 turns per coilLower resistance per path (−19 % / −36 %), wider wireNeeds about 11 % / 25 % longer stack for the same torque at 360 A

Design9795 · aluminium winding · Al end-winding multiplier 1.136

Drive cycle and range

Range is computed from energy per km at the motor terminals over two speed traces: the telematics log supplied earlier and WMTC Class 1. Range change = copper Wh/km ÷ aluminium Wh/km − 1, counting motor losses only.

Vehicle and method

  • Vehicle (given): GVW 757 kg, CdA 1.117 m², wheel radius 0.30 m, gear ratio 13.9. Assumed: rolling resistance 0.015, gearbox efficiency 0.95, rotating-mass factor 1.05, flat road.
  • Motor torque from road load and acceleration at each 1 s step; regenerative braking down to −26.4 N·m (largest regen torque in the log), friction brakes beyond.
  • Telematics: 10.75 km, 6363 steps (logging gaps skipped), motor up to 6908 rpm, 18 % of steps motoring. WMTC Class 1: 7.67 km, up to 6139 rpm.
  • The logged motor torque is negative even at cruise, so energy is computed from the speed trace through the vehicle model, not from the logged torque.
  • Losses are read from each design's own loss map (MTPA) at the cycle's speed and torque; points above a design's torque limit are held at the limit.
  • Inverter, battery and vehicle are the same for every design, so the battery-level range change is about the motor-level change.

Energies and losses in Wh/km at the motor (motor losses only; inverter, battery and vehicle are the same for every design).

Where the range goes

  • The cycles run mostly at light and medium torque below 6000 rpm. There, aluminium's higher DC resistance and the longer stacks' extra iron loss outweigh its lower AC loss.
  • Copper's AC winding loss over the telematics cycle is 0.84 Wh/km; aluminium's thin strands cut it to 0.22 Wh/km (recommended), but its DC loss rises from 2.82 to 3.40 Wh/km and iron loss from 3.04 to 4.21 Wh/km.
  • Each 1 % of range is about 0.61 Wh/km at the motor. Battery capacity was not given, so the battery cost of making up the range is not included.

Stator lamination
OD 160 → 167 mm. Slot depth 17.65 → 23.15 mm (slot bottom radius 71.15 → 76.65 mm). Yoke 8.85 → 6.85 mm. Tooth 15.54 → 14.54 mm. Unchanged: bore 107 mm, 12 slots, tooth tip, slot opening, slot-bottom corner radius, M235-35A 0.35 mm. Slot area 281.2 → 428.6 mm². New lamination die and housing bore.
Stack length
64 → 74 mm for stator, rotor laminations and magnets (same cross-sections). Shaft, bearing span and housing +10 mm.
Winding
Aluminium EC-1350, grade-2 enamel, 4 strands in hand × 1.90 mm (about 1.97 mm over enamel), 9 turns per coil, delta, 2 parallel paths, one coil per tooth. Fill 0.511 (copper 0.513). Mean turn 273.7 mm; 16.23 mΩ per path at 100 °C (copper 13.48).
Terminations
Welded or crimped joints with aluminium-rated lugs or Al-Cu transitions (no soldering), sealed against galvanic corrosion.
Drive
Same limits. New flux and resistance tables in the controller (flux and torque per amp ×1.041 against copper: stack × turns); aluminium temperature coefficient 0.00403/K.

Winding loss at peak torque 885 → 1055 W (+19 %), current density 15.2 → 9.2 A/mm². Check the peak duration in Motor-CAD Thermal. Design9795 · aluminium winding · Al end-winding multiplier 1.136

Assumptions and files

Limits of the study

  • 2D FEA; end effects only through the end-turn resistance and end-winding inductance.
  • Thermal behaviour not simulated; the higher winding loss at peak torque needs a Motor-CAD thermal check.
  • Aluminium wire fill held at copper's 0.513; a real aluminium winding with several strands may reach a different fill.
  • AC loss by the low-frequency hybrid method; for single wires near the skin depth (about 2.6 mm hot copper, 3.3 mm aluminium at 750 Hz) it is approximate.
  • Flux maps, demagnetisation, torque ripple and THD were not recomputed for these stator-only variants: the rotor is unchanged, and the slot opening and tooth tip are identical to copper's.
  • Costs are active materials only.
